questions.question:
Let $f : \left(2,4\right) \to ℝ$ be a differentiable function such that $\left(x{\log }_{e}x\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left({\log }_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) \ge 1,x \in \left(2,4\right)$ with $f\left(2\right) = \frac{1}{2}$ and $f\left(4\right) = \frac{1}{2}$.

Consider the following two statements:

(A) $f\left(x\right) \le 1,\text{for all}x \in \left(2,4\right)$

(B) $f\left(x\right) \ge 1 / 8,\text{for all}x \in \left(2,4\right)$

Then,
options: Neither statement $(A)$ nor statement $(B)$ is true
questions.explanation:
Given,

Domain and range of function,

$f : \left(2,4\right) \to ℝ \left(x{\log }_{e}x\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left({\log }_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) \ge 1,x \in \left(2,4\right) \implies \left(x{\log }_{e}x\right)\frac{d}{dx}f\left(x\right) + \left({\log }_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right)\frac{d}{dx}\left(x\right) + xf\left(x\right)\frac{d}{dx}\left({\log }_{e}x\right) \ge 1 \implies \frac{d}{dx}\left(x\ln xf\left(x\right)\right) \ge 1 \implies \frac{d}{dx}\left(x\ln xf\left(x\right)\right) \ge \frac{d}{dx}\left(x\right) \implies \frac{d}{dx}\left(x\ln xf\left(x\right) - x\right) \ge 0$

Hence, $h(x) = x\left(\ln x\right)f\left(x\right) - x$ is a increasing function,

$∴h(x) \ge h(2),x \in [2,4] \implies x\ln x \times f\left(x\right) - x \ge 2\ln 2 \times f\left(2\right) - 2 \implies x\ln xf(x) - x \ge \ln 2 - 2$

Similarly, $h\left(x\right) \le h\left(4\right) \implies x\ln xf\left(x\right) - x \le \ln 4 - 4$

So, $\frac{\ln 2 - 2}{x\ln x} + \frac{1}{\ln x} \le f(x) \le \frac{\ln 4 - 4}{x\ln x} + \frac{1}{\ln x}$

Now for $x \in \left(2,4\right) \frac{\ln 4 - 4}{x\ln x} + \frac{1}{\ln x} \le \frac{\ln 4 - 4}{2\ln 2} + \frac{1}{\ln 2} = 1 - \frac{1}{\ln 2} < 1 \implies f\left(x\right) \le 1\text{for}x \in \left(2,4\right)$

Now for $x \in \left(2,4\right) \frac{\ln 2 - 2}{x\ln x} + \frac{1}{\ln x} \ge \frac{\ln 2 - 2}{4\ln 4} + \frac{1}{\ln 4} = \frac{\ln 2 - 2}{4\ln 4} + \frac{1}{\ln 4} = \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{4\ln 2} > \frac{1}{8}$

Hence, $f(x) \ge \frac{1}{8}$

Hence both $A$ & $B$ are correct.

Hence, no such $f(x)$ exist.

So, $\alpha + \beta = 45$
